assessments.reasoning: Section 6.2 on printed and physical page 5 lists where open array types are admitted. Section 6.4 on printed and physical page 6 distinguishes fixed-size allocation from pointer allocation of an n-dimensional open array, requires n length expressions, and assigns the resulting pointer to the argument variable. The Proper procedures table in §10.3 on printed and physical page 17 specifies the integer argument types.

challenge.method: Compare omitted dimensions, fixed-array allocation, directly declared open-array variables and general parameter-only use. Visually inspect the Open array variables section of the independently fetched May 1991 ETH TR160 scan for conflicting spelling.
challenge.results: The 26-page report explicitly specifies pointer-based allocation and one integer length per dimension. The native ETH wrapper was byte-unstable relative to the frozen acquisition, but the independent page image at physical page 6, printed page 5, shows a direct ARRAY OF INTEGER variable and NEW(v,100), supporting the scoped historical distinction only. The wrapper did not qualify as exact-byte evidence.

limitations: The ETH note is earlier contextual material. The 26-page JKU report controls the claim. Allocation failure and behavior for invalid length values are outside the finding.
